title: Web scraping
game_role: When you enter the second region, your treasure clues appear.
objective: Collect titles, links and text from HTML pages with BeautifulSoup
story: The harbor's notice board is covered with announcements: ship times, prices, lost items... Copying them all into a notebook by hand would take hours. Web pages are notice boards like this. A program that reads a page and collects the useful information is doing **web scraping**.

sections.title: A quick look at HTML
sections.body:
Web pages are written in **HTML**. HTML marks content with tags: ```

Title

25 coins

Go to the map ``` - `

`, `

`, `` are tag names - `class="price"` and `href="/map"` are the tag's **attributes** - The text between the tags is the tag's text

sections.title: BeautifulSoup
sections.body: `BeautifulSoup` is a package that reads HTML and lets us search inside it: ```python from bs4 import BeautifulSoup soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") print(soup.title.text) # text of the tag first = soup.find("p") # the first <p> prices = soup.find_all("p", class_="price") # all price paragraphs link = soup.find("a")["href"] # an attribute's value ``` `class` is a special word in Python, so we add an underscore: `class_`

sections.title: In the real world
sections.body:
When scraping a real page, the page's HTML is first downloaded from the internet:

```python
import requests
html = requests.get("https://example.com").text
```

So that the examples work without an internet connection, we'll give the HTML as ready-made text. The scraping part works exactly the same way.

If BeautifulSoup isn't on your computer yet, install it first by typing `pip install beautifulsoup4` in the terminal (Day 20).

sections.title: Be a polite scraper
sections.body:
- Check whether a site allows scraping (its terms of use and its `robots.txt` file)
- Don't send hundreds of requests per second; you'll wear out the server
- Don't collect personal information
- If the site offers an **API**, use it instead of scraping (we'll see this on Day 28)

examples.title: Title and paragraphs
examples.code:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """ Harbor Board

Today's ships

The Seagull leaves at 10:00.

The Dolphin arrives at 14:30.

""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") print(soup.title.text) print(soup.find("h1").text) for p in soup.find_all("p"): print("-", p.text)

examples.title: Links
examples.code: from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = 'Map Ships' soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") for a in soup.find_all("a"): print(a.text, "->", a["href"])

examples.title: Find by class
examples.code:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Rope 5
  • Lantern 40
""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") prices = [int(s.text) for s in soup.find_all("span", class_="price")] print(prices, "total:", sum(prices))

tasks.title: Add up the prices
tasks.prompt: Add up the numbers in all the tags with `class="price"` and store the result in `total`.
tasks.starter:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Rope 5
  • Lantern 40
  • Map 15
    • """ soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") total = 0 print("Total:", total)
tasks.solution:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Rope 5
  • Lantern 40
  • Map 15
    • """ soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") total = sum([int(s.text) for s in soup.find_all(class_="price")]) print("Total:", total)
hints: The texts are strings; turn them into numbers with int() before adding.

challenge.title: Read the table
challenge.prompt: Put every row of the HTML table into the `rows` list as a `(name, score)` tuple. Skip the header row and make the score an int.
challenge.starter:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
NameScore
Piko300
Emma250
""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") rows = [] print(rows)
challenge.solution:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
NameScore
Piko300
Emma250
""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") rows = [] for tr in soup.find_all("tr"): cells = tr.find_all("td") if len(cells) == 2: rows.append((cells[0].text, int(cells[1].text))) print(rows)
hints: Each row is a <tr>. Its cells: tr.find_all("td")
The header row has <th>, not <td>, so it comes back empty.

project_task.title: Treasure clues
project_task.prompt:
Treasure clues are hidden on an old page at the harbor. Only the items with `class="clue"` are real clues; the others are traps!

- Put the texts of the real clues into the `clues` list, in order.
- Then print them numbered, like `1. Go to the lighthouse`.
project_task.starter:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Go to the lighthouse
  • Enter the cave
  • Walk three steps north
  • Look under the red stone
""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") clues = [] # print them numbered
project_task.solution:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Go to the lighthouse
  • Enter the cave
  • Walk three steps north
  • Look under the red stone
""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") clues = [li.text.strip() for li in soup.find_all("li", class_="clue")] for i, clue in enumerate(clues, 1): print(f"{i}. {clue}")
